purpose: Twenty useful starting guides for individually named Alaska communities and governments, with selected community, historical, language, educational and environmental accounts plus specifically relevant credited imagery. People, governments and corporations remain distinct.

profiles.name: Cheesh-Na Tribe
profiles.regionalPriority: Individually scoped Alaska community and government routes
remainingGaps: This is a bounded introduction to education and planning, not a complete village history.
No language recordings, grant outcomes audit or current programme schedule was reviewed.
The historical airfield image supplies named-place context only; it does not depict the Tribal government or all Chistochina residents.

profiles.name: Gulkana Village Council
profiles.regionalPriority: Individually scoped Alaska community and government routes
remainingGaps: The reviewed plan remains a January 2024 public review draft; later adoption and project completion were not checked.
Early settlement dates and present land title/access are not resolved by this introduction.
The 1914 photograph is a bridge near Gulkana, not a portrait of the present village or a photograph of the 1943 bridge project.

profiles.name: Mentasta Traditional Council
profiles.regionalPriority: Individually scoped Alaska community and government routes
remainingGaps: The two substantive works are reused from the existing Ahtna collection with their original review dates and scope retained.
Audio playback, current teaching availability and learning outcomes were not audited.
The 1943 NPS photograph is a historical view of Mentasta Lake, not an image of the Council, residents or a precise homeland boundary.

profiles.name: Native Village of Gakona
profiles.regionalPriority: Individually scoped Alaska community and government routes
remainingGaps: The village’s historical development and language teaching need additional community-directed sources.
No linked site assessment, laboratory findings, current environmental conditions or post-2025 results were reviewed.
The Copper River photograph is explicitly labeled Gakona in its source; it supplies narrow landscape context, not a representation of every resident or the government.

profiles.name: Native Village of Tazlina
profiles.regionalPriority: Individually scoped Alaska community and government routes
remainingGaps: The source set needs a fuller village-authored history and contemporary educational account.
Current legal ownership, access, environmental safety and ecological outcomes were not independently reviewed.
The historical photograph provides named Tazlina River context only; it does not show the village site, confluence, Tribal property or current environmental conditions.

profiles.name: Chickaloon Native Village
profiles.regionalPriority: Individually scoped Alaska community and government routes
remainingGaps: A focused starting guide, with two reviewed community works; it is not a comprehensive history.
The brief history’s recognition-date sentence was not used to reconstruct legal chronology.
Additional public oral histories, authored scholarship and dated program reports remain to be reviewed; restricted archive materials were not accessed.

profiles.name: Native Village of Chitina
profiles.regionalPriority: Individually scoped Alaska community and government routes
remainingGaps: Direct tribal-government narrative and contemporary program sources remain a significant gap.
The reviewed state study is a selected historical passage; current fishery rules, land title, resource locations and harvesting advice are not assessed.
Historical biographies are presently represented by a corporation account and need additional community-directed and primary-record reading.

profiles.name: Eklutna Native Village
profiles.regionalPriority: Individually scoped Alaska community and government routes
remainingGaps: The reviewed pages are community accounts, not a comprehensive history or legal assessment.
Language-specific materials and additional publicly shared oral histories remain to be reviewed.
Current flow conditions, project decisions and restoration results require dated records beyond these undated program pages.

profiles.name: Kenaitze Indian Tribe
profiles.regionalPriority: Individually scoped Alaska community and government routes
remainingGaps: The two works provide a focused introduction to living institutions and language priorities; earlier history remains limited.
Linked dictionaries, recordings, constitutional records and program reports remain to be reviewed individually.
Current enrollment, speaker numbers, health outcomes and program effectiveness are not assessed.

profiles.name: Douglas Indian Association
profiles.regionalPriority: Individually scoped Alaska community and government routes
remainingGaps: A focused introduction based on the Tribe’s own public works; no full-history claim is made.
Additional public first-person narratives, language materials and archival records remain to be reviewed.
Current environmental conditions, health implications, land title and legal outcomes are outside this guide.

profiles.name: Angoon Community Association
profiles.regionalPriority: Individually scoped Alaska community and government routes
remainingGaps: This guide reviews a small, dated source set and does not supply a complete history.
The selected testimony is an opening portion of a letter, not the entire hearing.
A sustained Association-directed account of language work, community priorities and historical change remains to be located.

profiles.name: Hoonah Indian Association
profiles.regionalPriority: Individually scoped Alaska community and government routes
remainingGaps: HIA’s pages are undated; officeholders, schedules and program outcomes were not inferred.
The source set emphasizes Glacier Bay and needs fuller local language, educational and economic history.
Ceremonial accounts, harvest instructions, artworks and linked media were not used.

profiles.name: Organized Village of Kake
profiles.regionalPriority: Individually scoped Alaska community and government routes
remainingGaps: The historical statement is selected-body review; its cited forthcoming book was not read.
The culture-camp example is dated 2020, with no present outcome claim.
Cannery rehabilitation is treated as a documented goal, not a verified finished project.

profiles.name: Metlakatla Indian Community, Annette Island Reserve
profiles.regionalPriority: Individually scoped Alaska community and government routes
remainingGaps: A fuller community-directed founding and migration history remains needed.
Only selected parts of the 75-page plan were reviewed; maps, legal boundary conclusions and inventory calculations were excluded.
Language-program goals are not treated as evaluated outcomes or as proof of fluency for all residents.

profiles.name: Native Village of Tatitlek
profiles.regionalPriority: Individually scoped Alaska community and government routes
remainingGaps: The two community accounts are undated and come from distinct Native institutions rather than the IRA Council itself.
The guide needs further tribal-government-directed history and public language resources.
No present population, membership, territorial, harvest, legal-power or program-outcome conclusions are made.

profiles.name: Craig Tribal Association
profiles.regionalPriority: Individually scoped Alaska community and government routes
remainingGaps: This short guide needs additional Association-directed historical, language and contemporary community accounts.
The linked Shaan-Seet text and underlying Elder oral histories were not independently read.
Additional Association-directed sources are needed for contemporary cultural and environmental activities.

profiles.name: Hydaburg Cooperative Association
profiles.regionalPriority: Individually scoped Alaska community and government routes
remainingGaps: Find newer community reports on the library and language initiatives.
Read further Haida-authored historical perspectives without generalizing one account to all Haida communities.

profiles.name: Klawock Cooperative Association
profiles.regionalPriority: Individually scoped Alaska community and government routes
remainingGaps: Seek additional Association-authored contemporary histories and cultural accounts.
Review fuller community voices and later education reports; current legal or membership questions need current primary records.

profiles.name: Organized Village of Kasaan
profiles.regionalPriority: Individually scoped Alaska community and government routes
remainingGaps: Seek further community-authored historical and language accounts.
Check later public updates for the library relocation and transportation plans; no current access promise is made.
No adopted/final version of the August 2025 public-review draft was established in this source review.

profiles.name: Ketchikan Indian Community
profiles.regionalPriority: Individually scoped Alaska community and government routes
remainingGaps: Read additional KIC-authored language and historical materials.
Distinguish dated institutional statements, wider town history and individual experiences; do not infer current statistics or membership.

limits: Selected works and frames only; source scopes and dates control. Historical or river/landscape images are narrow context, not current-member portraits or territorial boundaries. No community endorsement or exhaustive-history claim.
